master.description: The master graph: what the sources observed. Pods, services, deployments and nodes of the clusters, the Azure resources, calls between pods, meters, warning, activity and audit events, and the authored capabilities, rules and policies.

deploymentHealth.description: The Deployments of the workload and the traffic between them, each with a state: a Deployment is Healthy while enough of its pods are ready.

deploymentReport.description: A report on the health of the Deployments as a document: counts and one line per Deployment.

serviceTree.description: The service tree: the services of each namespace and who calls whom, lifted from the calls between their pods.

capabilities.description: The business capabilities and the calls between them, lifted from the calls between the services that realize them.

treeSignals.description: The signals of the estate: each meter of an element read against the authored rules that name it, with its state.

treeStructure.description: The tree structure: elements and their parents, from the Azure resource ids and the Kubernetes objects of the master. A cluster that is an Azure resource is one element with the Kubernetes subtree below it.

treeRollup.description: The roll-up policy of every element, and the edges the roll-up follows: an element whose policy is ignore does not roll up what is below it.

healthTree.description: The health tree: every element of the estate under its parent, with its own state and the state rolled up from what is below it.

healthReport.description: A report on the health tree as a document: the elements that are not healthy and why.

workloadStructure.description: What is my workload made of, what does it talk to, and what does each part depend on? The services of one namespace with their deployments and pods, the nodes, pools and cluster they run on, and the Azure resources they use, with each dependency's evidence.

workload.description:
Is my workload healthy, and if not, which part is to blame? Each component's state is the worst severity over everything that affects it: what it contains and what it depends on, up to sixteen edges away.
Its own severity comes from its signals: each meter of an Azure resource or a node and the warning events of each pod, read against the authored rules. A pod's warnings are 0 in every minute in which its source reported without one; a meter that has not reported for five minutes is in no data.
A pod also counts the node it runs on; a deployment is unhealthy only when at least half of its pods are (degraded when at least half are degraded or worse). No data counts above healthy and below degraded; a component that nothing measured is Unknown. An observed call carries no failure.
